candidates: §3.2 lists `dane`, arguably English — refuted: English "Dane" is a capitalized proper noun, so rule 2's lowercase-English-word test is not tripped.

Function words `dla oraz przy bez przed wedlug jako` contradict rule 3's "not general Polish" — refuted: rule 3 qualifies the target as "words an agent would emit when naming a change", which Polish connectives inside change descriptions are.

§1 promises "one reject + one accept vector per integration surface" while §7 gives create_branch two accept vectors — refuted: §1 is a scope summary and §7 is the normative testing section whose set is a strict superset; no conflict.

§3's lowercasing means the reported token loses original casing, clashing with §7's "exact" message vectors for mixed-case `Naprawa` — refuted: §3 unambiguously settles it (lowercase input, returns the matching set member), so the sections agree.

D3's gloss "(ref names, log subjects, PR list titles)" overstates versus §4's "never `id`" — refuted: §1 Out of scope explicitly exempts the `id` segment, so the gloss is a category description the spec itself resolves.

AC-1's "rejections record zero git/gh calls" is not asserted for the av_commit vector in §7 — refuted: §4 states all three checks are pure TypeScript with zero process spawns, so AC-1 is a consistent superset, not a contradiction.

§1's premise "existing charsets reject diacritics" versus the `[^a-z0-9]+` tokenizer silently shredding diacritic words — refuted: verifying the charsets requires repo facts (feasibility lens); inside the spec the premise and rule 1 agree.

§4's "Runs after Conventional-Commits header check" could preempt the §7 vector `"fix: naprawa logowania"` — refuted: that vector carries a valid conventional header, so the ordering never suppresses the English error.
§7's collision sample lists `test` while rule 2 excludes `testy` — refuted: different tokens, neither is in §3.2, no contradiction.
§8's "any hit is correctable by removing the token" versus §3.1 being binding on "every future addition" — refuted: removal is not an addition, so the curation rules are untouched.
av_commit target could be read as the whole first line vs. only the text after `type(scope):` — refuted by §4's explicit "first line of the trimmed message (subject)".

Case of the token in the exact error message (`"Naprawa"` vs `"naprawa"`) — refuted: §3 lowercases before splitting and membership requires a lowercase set entry, so the returned token is necessarily lowercase.
§3.2 lists `stare`, which §3.1 rule 2 forbids (an English word) — out of this lens (internal consistency of the list, not an ambiguity or an uncheckable criterion).
§4's "Runs after S3–S8" leaves S1–S2 unmentioned — refuted: S9 running last after the sequential S-rules is derivable and produces no observable divergence.
AC-4's "`dist/` is synced" is unmeasurable — refuted: checkable by rebuilding and diffing `dist/`; a standing repo convention, not a spec ambiguity.
"zero recorded git calls" / "zero recorded runner calls" / "zero git/gh calls" phrasing drift across §7 and §9 — refuted: all three denote the same mocked-runner assertion; wording only.
§6's doctrine sentence is a line-wrapped blockquote while AC-3 requires the docs to "contain the doctrine sentence" — refuted: it is a prose-doc check and line wrapping is formatting, not content.
Whether §3.2 is exhaustive for v1 or a seed to extend — refuted by the heading "Initial token list (normative)" plus §8's "extensible one token at a time", which scopes additions to the future.
Whether the av_commit gate throws or returns an error result — refuted: §1 says it "rejects the call with an instructive error" and AC-1 says "throws".
Diacritic input is shredded by the `/[^a-z0-9]+/` split — refuted: §3.1 rule 1 records that upstream charsets already reject diacritics, so the case is unreachable for the gated fields.
Ambiguity over whether S9 sees the raw or normalized description / the id — refuted: §4 says "normalized `description` (never `id`)" and §7 pins it with the `ZMIANA-12` vector.

`stare` in §3.2's function-words list is an English word and so violates §3.1 rule 2's own ban — a real defect, but it is the list contradicting its own binding rule, which is internal-consistency's mandate, not a missing design decision.

Case of the token echoed in the error templates (`"Naprawa"` vs `"naprawa"`) — derivable: §3 states the function "lowercases the input" before splitting, so the returned token is necessarily lowercase.

camelCase evasion (`NaprawaBledu` lowercases to one unlisted token and passes) — the tokenization algorithm is fully specified, so no implementer divergence; §1 labels the stoplist "an explicitly incomplete heuristic" and §8 accepts recall gaps.
Non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic/CJK) tokenize to nothing under `/[^a-z0-9]+/` and pass unchecked — same accepted-heuristic disclaimer in §1/§8; no design decision is missing.
Agents can bypass the gate entirely by invoking `git commit` through bash — explicitly out of scope per §1 ("Any change to git invocation contracts, guards, or the bash policy").
No runtime override/escape hatch for a false-positive hit — §8 states the remedy ("any hit is correctable by removing the token"), so the absence of an override is a recorded decision, not a gap.

Placement of the §6 doctrine sentence is specified only for `AGENTS.md` ("conventions section") and not for the other three files — docs placement is implementation-plan detail and AC-3 makes the outcome checkable.

The exact membership of the "~50 common English dev words" sample is elided with "…" — a test fixture's literal contents are implementation-plan detail my mandate forbids demanding (the separate reported gap is the absent enforcement rule for future additions, not the sample's exact words).
§7 locates only the module test file (`tests/modules/commit/english-policy.test.ts`) and not the per-surface vector files — test file layout is implementation-plan detail.

Whether the `av_commit` subject check covers the Conventional-Commit type/scope or only the description after the colon — §4 answers it ("first line of the trimmed message"); the surviving defect is the missing identifier exemption, reported separately.
Multiple offending tokens force repeated agent round-trips since only the first is reported — §3 explicitly decides this ("returns the **first** token").
Ordering of the new checks relative to existing rules is unstated — §4's "Runs after" column pins all three (S3–S8, the Conventional-Commits header check, T3).
Whether rejection is a hard error or a recoverable result — AC-1 states every reject vector "throws its exact normative message", and D4 presumes agent retry.

av_commit rejection leaves the whole tree staged (git add runs first) — refuted as a new defect: the existing Conventional-Commits rejection at the same hook already behaves that way; only the false zero-spawn/AC-1 claim survives.
S9 placed inside the shared validateSegmentRules would also gate `id` — refuted: the §4 table says "normalized `description` (never `id`)" explicitly, so the exemption is unambiguous.

S9 ordering vs the composed-name rules N1–N11 is unspecified — refuted: "Runs after S3–S8" plus composeBranchName's existing structure (validateSegmentRules then validateBranchName) already fixes S9 before the N rules.

§7's "passes existing AC-3 flow unchanged" looked like a dangling reference now that docs/specs holds only this spec — refuted: tests/modules/commit/create-pr.test.ts:358 names the test "AC-3: happy path", so the reference resolves in-repo.

Conventional-Commits scope is inside the gated subject line, so a Polish-named scope is rejected with no `id`-style exemption — refuted: §3.2 targets change vocabulary, scope names are author-controlled, and §8 accepts false positives with a token-removal remedy.

New stoplist could break existing test vectors — refuted: existing vectors ("fix alert dialog", "release/2026.07.21", "update dependencies", "memory leak in auth", "simplify parser", "readme update") contain no listed token.
The new english-policy.ts module might need build-entry registration — refuted: tsup.root.config.ts entry is `src/**/*.ts`, so the file is built automatically.
AC-4's "dist/ is synced" is not enforced by `bun run check` — refuted: `check` runs `build`, which regenerates the tracked dist, and `verify-dist` exists as a separate script.
toLowerCase() locale hazards and ReadonlySet availability — refuted: target es2022 provides ReadonlySet and non-locale toLowerCase is deterministic for the ASCII list.
§3.2 tokens violating the ≥3-char/`^[a-z0-9]{3,}$` invariant — refuted: the shortest listed tokens are `dla` and `bez` (3 chars) and all entries are lowercase ASCII letters.
`lista`, `raport`, `adres` are near-English and risk false positives — refuted: §3.1 rule 2 explicitly admits them and none is an English spelling.
AC-1 says "Every §4 reject vector" while the vectors actually live in §7 — out of lens (cross-reference wording, internal-consistency/ambiguity territory), not a platform-feasibility defect.

Casing of `<token>` in the three error templates ("Naprawa" vs "naprawa") is unspecified — refuted: §3 lowercases the input before splitting and every set entry is lowercase per §3.1 rule 1, so the returned and emitted token is necessarily lowercase; derivable, not ambiguous.

Diacritic-written non-English input bypasses the gate because `/[^a-z0-9]+/` makes diacritics separators — refuted: §1 asserts "The existing charsets reject diacritics" and §3.1 rule 1 records that assumption explicitly; validating the premise against the code is the feasibility lens's job, not a contract defect.

`dane` collides with English "Dane" — refuted: §3.1 rule 2 targets words "spelled identically in Polish and English" as ordinary English words; "Dane" is a capitalized proper noun and is not a lowercase English common word.

av_commit gate scope ambiguous between the whole first line and only the description after `type(scope):` — refuted: §4's table names the gated field as "first line of the trimmed message", with "(subject)" as a gloss on that phrase, so a description-only reading contradicts the normative text.

The av_commit error carries no rule id while S9/T4 do, making the three-message error contract inconsistent — refuted: §4 marks that row "— (plain sentence)" and states S9/T4 "extend their families' fixed templates", so the per-family shape is a deliberate, recorded choice.

Reporting only the first offending token forces multiple reject/retry round trips — refuted: §3 explicitly specifies returning the **first** token and D4's fixed hint instructs translating the whole field, so a single retry resolves all hits.

`ReadonlySet<string>` is compile-time only, so the exported stoplist is runtime-mutable by a casting consumer — refuted: no stated invariant requires runtime immutability and no implementer divergence follows; nit-level pedantry.

The JSON-encoding site for `<token>` (module vs. each call site) is unspecified — refuted: §3 fixes the module's return as the raw token and the emitted string is byte-identical either way; pure implementation detail.
§1 names both the `id` segment and `taskId` as create_branch exemptions, blurring the parameter contract — refuted: both are out of scope under either reading, so no observable behavior differs.
§4's File column gives bare filenames without directories — refuted: §1 and §5 pin the module under `src/modules/commit/`, making the paths derivable.

§3.1 rule 1 says tokens are "lowercase ASCII" while §7's invariant regex `/^[a-z0-9]{3,}$/` admits digits — refuted: no listed entry contains a digit and the looser regex cannot reject a rule-1-compliant list; no behavioral divergence.

No versioning marker or caller escape hatch for a future false positive in the exported set — refuted: §8 explicitly accepts this risk and states the correction path ("any hit is correctable by removing the token").

Asserting full error strings freezes the message contract against future wording changes — refuted: §4 states this intentionally ("the hint text never varies, so tests can assert the full message exactly").
